leftEvidence.title: God presents the chosen servant in whom he delights

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: God presents a chosen servant, delights in him, and puts his Spirit on him for justice among the nations.
points.right: After six days Jesus takes three disciples up a high mountain; his face shines, his clothes become white, and Moses and Elijah appear speaking with him.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: The servant acts without crushing what is weak and becomes covenant and light.
points.right: Peter proposes three tents; a bright cloud overshadows them, the voice names the beloved Son and commands listening, and the frightened disciples finally see Jesus alone.

payload.posture: Divine delight language makes Isaiah 42 material evidence for hearing Matthew’s voice.

rightEvidence.title: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John

payload.tension: The mountain voice is not a verbatim quotation of the complete servant passage.
payload.title: The delighted servant and the beloved Son
